title: A Thousand Mountains | Lugu Lake
subtitle: For a faraway friend who listens to me attentively.
body:
Ten years ago, would you have believed it?

None of the sunsets we missed have perished,

Romance does not necessarily require two figures side by side,

You will love in confusion, and you will love absurdly,

And you will fall in love with Don Juan’s light without the lights turned on,

You said it: in the end, it is not home;

Perhaps I am wandering—who is not wandering?

There has been hesitation, there has been wildness,

And what I want is the ordinary;

All different, the time that was wasted,

Standing on the opposite shore of the lake,

We walk toward the moon, forgetting a little of the past.

Loving flight in dreams, and loving electric sheep too,

Unable to resist wandering all day,

You said it: all you want is a heartbeat;

Barren poems, the distance we cannot resist,

Hermann Hesse, Sarasate,

Who is it that wants to wander?

Exactly the same, the time we waste,

Standing on the opposite shore of the lake,

We walk toward the moon, forgetting a little of the past.

We walk toward the moon, forgetting a little of the past.

Ten years from now, would you believe it?

None of the sunsets that perished were missed,

Two figures side by side do not necessarily require mance-ro.[1]

---

[1] The last line reverses the Chinese phonetic halves of “romantic,” 罗曼蒂克, into 蒂克罗曼. “Mance-ro” preserves that reversal rather than smoothing away the wordplay. “Electric sheep” recalls Philip K. Dick’s *Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?*
